title: 1,000 YEARS?
sub: Vietnamese historiography traditionally dates the main period of Chinese rule from 111 BC to 939 AD. About a thousand years. What did that mean?
say: Vietnamese historiography traditionally dates the main period of Chinese rule from one hundred eleven B C to nine thirty-nine A D. About a thousand years. What did that mean?

title: 111 BC
sub: In 111 BC, the Han conquered Nanyue, a kingdom that had included the Red River region. Vietnamese histories often use this as their starting point.
say: In one hundred eleven B C, the Han conquered Nahn-yweh, a kingdom that had included the Red River region. Vietnamese histories often use this as their starting point.

title: NOT ALL OF VIETNAM
sub: It did not cover today's Vietnam. Chinese administration centered on the Red River region and nearby areas.
say: It did not cover today's Vietnam. Chinese administration centered on the Red River region and nearby areas.

title: WITH BREAKS
sub: And it was not unbroken. The Trưng sisters' revolt briefly interrupted Han rule around the year 40. Han forces restored control by 43. Later, Lý Bôn founded the state of Vạn Xuân in 544. Sui forces reconquered it in 602.
say: And it was not unbroken. The Chung sisters' revolt briefly interrupted Han rule around the year forty. Han forces restored control by forty-three. Later, Lee Bone founded the state of Vahn Swun in five forty-four. Sui forces reconquered it in six oh two.

sub: In 938, Ngô Quyền defeated a Southern Han fleet at the Bạch Đằng River. He established the Ngô dynasty in 939.
say: In nine thirty-eight, Ngoh Kwee-en defeated a Southern Han fleet at the Bahk Dahng River. He established the Ngoh dynasty in nine thirty-nine.

title: WHAT STAYED
sub: Literary Chinese later remained important in government and scholarship for centuries. Meanwhile the region's spoken languages, including the ancestors of Vietnamese, carried on.
say: Literary Chinese later remained important in government and scholarship for centuries. Meanwhile the region's spoken languages, including the ancestors of Vietnamese, carried on.

title: WHO WERE THEY?
sub: Who were the people of the delta? Some scholars caution that modern labels like Chinese and Vietnamese do not fit these early identities neatly.

title: TWO VIEWS
sub: Chinese records described the region through imperial administration. Some modern histories frame the period as a thousand-year struggle. Historians debate that framing.
